answer: A graph-based trust protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by bounding message flow along credit paths between vetted peers. Whether dispatching couriers with timber or deploying sensors across a rock ledge, agents require bilateral trust links to transact. An adversary cannot mirror artificial routes and must expend the scarce, verifiable cost of securing genuine counterparty credit per identity. However, this topology isolates benign newcomers and favors entrenched agent clusters.
